ma_q_wall.blurb: Q Wall is a compact, fairly steep face in the old granite workings at Quincy Quarries, a short drive south of Boston. It stands around a hundred feet and sits opposite another face in the same pit. Most of the twelve climbs are top-ropes, with a pair of trad lines, one bolted line and a single boulder problem. Grades start around 5.6 and 5.7 and run through the 5.10s and 5.11s into the low 5.12 range, so there is something for a beginner and a few lines for strong climbers. Fill added over the years makes getting to the base easy.

ma_big_twin.blurb: Big Twin is the larger of the two boulders that make up The Twins, in Gilbert Hills State Forest in Foxborough, southwest of Boston. You meet it second along the trail in from the High Rock entrance, and it holds the better problems of the pair. All twelve lines are bouldering, running from an easy V1 up to V7, with a handful in the middle grades around V3 to V5 and a couple of harder tests. A mix of cracks, aretes and a dyno makes it a good stop for a short session within a bigger day exploring the park's many other blocks.

ma_beehive_boulders.blurb: Beehive Boulders is a single large block on the North Side of Dykes Pond in Gloucester, on Cape Ann, not far from the highway. It holds twelve bouldering problems from V2 up to V6; the biggest group sits at V4, with a few at V5 and V6 and only a couple of easier ones. The walk from the trailhead is short: a few minutes of narrow path once the pond comes into view. The wider North Side has one of the best concentrations of quality boulders on Cape Ann, so this block pairs well with other stops nearby.

ma_millenium_boulder.blurb: Millenium Boulder is the big block that greets you when you walk into The Hideaway, one of the two bouldering zones near Montague in western Massachusetts. The gneiss starts out overhanging and then eases to a slab up top, giving a wide spread of styles. Twelve problems climb it, from an easy V0 to a hard V11, but the bulk are serious: half fall between V5 and V8 and several more reach V9 and V10. It suits strong boulderers more than beginners, though a couple of friendly lines exist, and it can be combined with the nearby cliff band and the adjacent Happy Valley.

ma_14th_hole_boulder.blurb: The 14th Hole Boulder is one golden block standing right on the fourteenth hole of the golf course in Lynn Woods, north of Boston. It sits in the Golf Course Area, a medium walk from the main lot rather than a quick stop. The twelve problems are all bouldering and cover a wide range, from a V0 warm-up through the low and middle grades, with most in the V2 to V6 band and one line reaching V7. That makes it a handy block for a mixed group. Lynn Woods is known for coarse granite and short, clean lines.
